text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Initial plan for gemm_128x4096x4096 (M=128,N=K=4096, FP16 inputs, FP32 accum). Allowed domains cover block_M 32/64/128 (all divide M=128), block_N 64/128 (divide N=4096), block_K 32/64 (divide K=4096), num_stages 1-3, threads fixed at 128, and swizzle restricted to [0] per instruction to establish a row-major baseline. Shared-memory cap set to 32768 bytes to respect the hard portability cap for Mac Metal vs GB10; estimated footprint per candidate = max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N), with epilogue buffer aliasing assumed. Objective weights are equal (1) across traffic, launches, pipeline and footprint to keep the first comparison unbiased. Hypothesis/history: no prior evaluations, so no exclusions applied and domains kept broad within the allowed sets; the next hypothesis to test is whether analytic swizzle reuse (serpentine panels) actually lowers simulator traffic/latency for this tall-skinny M=128 shape, which is why later rounds will open swizzle to [0,4,8,16]; the tall-skinny GEMM has very few M-tiles (ceil(128/block_M) in {1,2,4}), so launch and reuse effects on block_M may dominate and weights may be revisited after feedback. This proxy cost is dimensionless and only used for ranking, never interpreted as microseconds; Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR but do not run the CUDA binary, and GB10 values are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements."}
